correctness.rationale: Algebraically eliminate the symmetric prime-two equation to a reciprocal quartic, then a quadratic in \(2\cos(2\pi s)\). Both roots are in (-2,2). Positivity and determinant one of all Jacobians force every two-step fixed point to be nondegenerate, so compact implicit continuation preserves exactly five points from the cat limit; a monotone scalar fixed-point equation identifies the unique ordinary fixed point. The remaining four are the stated two-cycles. The Jacobian is the same at antipodal orbit points, yielding exact eigenvalue radicals. First-order Taylor expansions at \(\mu=0\) and \(\varepsilon=1-\mu\) give slope 1 and endpoint square-root coefficients. The packaged verification program independently checks the critical identities and high-precision examples; finite checks are not used to prove universal assertions.

value.rationale: The exact all-prime-two orbit census and separate unstable multiplier spectra are natural dynamical invariants of the original smooth Anosov family. The proved strict same-period expansion inequality and two unequal square-root boundary constants directly quantify hyperbolicity nonuniformity discussed numerically in the 2024 anchor, rather than giving a routine selected-point computation. The universal edge ratio \(1+\sqrt2\) is absent from the original fixed-point trace and transfer-operator spectra. The result has intrinsic use in comparing periodic-data rigidity and singular hyperbolic degeneration, without asserting any new global bundle-regularity theorem.
